title: Cap both expected query and scalar work costs with a paid TV budget
statement: Suppose a fully constructive original-oracle sampler has TV<=1/20 and known computable expectations EN<=A exp(aL^(1/3)), EW<=A d^p exp(aL^(1/3)), where W counts ALL scalar operations and continuous random draws. Abort to0 before exceeding Nmax=ceil(80A exp(aL^(1/3))) or Wmax=ceil(80A d^p exp(aL^(1/3))). Markov plus a union bound gives abort probability<=1/40. Coupling capped and uncapped runs gives total TV<=1/20+1/40=3/40<1/10. Known constants can be absorbed into one larger computable universal C for d>=2, including polynomial local overhead. This makes both caps EVERY-run. It does not construct the assumed expected sharp-scale sampler and does not turn a d^(1/5) upper bound into subpolynomial queries. The earlier Root generic constant-TV truncation insight is credited once; this is its explicit two-budget interface.

This exceeds the requested sharp scale. Conditional capping pays BOTH query and local-work/random-draw bounds; ideal stronger-oracle or published conditional RGO guarantees are never treated as an available implementation.
